subject: Follow-up: Private deployment vs public cloud — network & control plane clarifications
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Andrew Cole <andrew.cole@fininsights.com>
Cc: procurement@fininsights.com
Date: 2027-05-09T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Private deployment vs public cloud — network & control plane clarifications

Hi Andrew,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the candid run-through of FinInsights' constraints. Quick recap + next steps so everyone is aligned: 

Summary of FinInsights constraints we captured
- Must run inference inside an air-gapped subnet for selected models (PII-sensitive scoring).
- Control plane traffic must be restricted to a customer-managed VPC endpoint or offline bundle deployment.
- Procurement prefers minimal cross-account networking changes; prefer outbound-only whitelisting if possible.

Redwood differentiators relevant to this eval (short)
- Private control plane option: can be run as a customer-managed control plane inside your VPC (no internet egress for model run-time telemetry).
- Air-gap installation: our on-prem appliance supports offline model packaging and local-only download.
- Smart routing & fallbacks: when capacity constrained, we can route to a cheaper model variant within the same private env; no external cloud hops.

Immediate asks / next tests we propose
1) Network test: please confirm whether a single outbound HTTPS allow to our controlplane-repo endpoint is acceptable (we can provide an IP range and a signed bundle alternative).
2) Proof points: we will send a short network segmentation checklist and a sample offline bundle to demonstrate air-gap install flow.
3) SE deep-dive: loop in your infra SEs for a 60-90m technical session (recommended attendees: infra, security, network).

I attached a diagram and a checklist to get started. If procurement needs a security/architecture letter for the RFP, we can provide one next week.

Proposed timeline: send checklist today (attached), SE call next Tuesday (05/11) or Wednesday (05/12).

Next step from your side: confirm whether outbound-only allow to a signed bundle URL is feasible and who from infra to invite to the SE call.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Camila.Reyes@redwood.ai

Thanks Camila — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Procurement note: we need the security/architecture letter for the RFP by COB Friday (05/14). Can you commit to that?
- Network constraints: outbound-only HTTPS to a fixed IP range is acceptable, but we cannot allow DNS-based whitelisting to public hostnames.
- Air-gap: we need to know if the offline bundle requires HSM for signing verification or whether a SHA256 checksum is sufficient. Our security team will need to sign off.

I'll confirm attendees for the SE call by EOD Monday. Please include an agenda for the technical session so we can route it to the right folks.

Regards,

Hi team / Andrew,

Short answers up front:
- Offline bundle validation: we support both HSM-signed images (recommended) and SHA256 checksums. For highest assurance, our signing workflow can integrate with customer HSMs; we will provide verification tooling that validates HSM signatures locally (no outbound traffic required for verification).
- Control plane egress: when running Redwood Private with a customer-managed control plane hosted inside your VPC, runtime telemetry and model updates can be configured to use only an outbound allow to a fixed IP range (we can publish a CIDR block). Telemetry can be disabled entirely in locked-down installs.
- DNSless allow: we will provide static IP ranges and also an option to deliver a fully self-contained air-gap bundle if network-level outbound is disallowed.

Proposed SE call agenda (60 min):
1) Quick intros & goals (5m)
2) Infra constraints and desired attacker model (10m)
3) Network flows & allowed opens (15m) — we will show CIDR ranges + port list
4) Demo: air-gap bundle install and local validation (15m)
5) Q&A and procurement checklist review (15m)

Deliverables before the call:
- Security/architecture letter (Camila owner) — draft by 05/14 COB
- Control plane CIDRs + port list (attached matrix) — attached: controlplane-interop-matrix.csv
- Offline bundle steps + HSM integration notes (attached in diagram + short doc)

Attachments:
- controlplane-interop-matrix.csv (CSV, 3KB)
- additional-airgap-notes.txt (TXT, 2KB)

If that agenda looks good Andrew, propose Tuesday 05/11 at 11:00am PT for the workshop. If you need a longer deep-dive we can extend to 90m.

Thanks,
